corpus.text: Epistemic stability measures the coherence of knowledge representations over time and under perturbation. A stable epistemic system maintains consistent beliefs when exposed to noise or conflicting evidence.
Bayesian reasoning provides a principled framework for updating beliefs given new evidence. The posterior probability is proportional to the likelihood times the prior.
Knowledge graphs represent entities and their relationships as directed graphs. Nodes are entities, edges represent typed relationships between them.

Uncertainty quantification is the process of characterizing and reducing the uncertainty in computational models and data. Aleatoric uncertainty arises from inherent randomness, epistemic uncertainty from lack of knowledge.
Causal inference distinguishes correlation from causation. The do-calculus allows reasoning about interventions in causal graphs, enabling prediction of the effects of actions.
Formal epistemology applies mathematical tools to the study of knowledge, belief, and rational inference. Modal logic extends propositional logic with possibility and necessity operators.

The free energy principle posits that biological systems minimize surprise by updating their internal models of the world. This unifies perception, action, and learning under a single variational objective.

Topology studies properties of spaces that are preserved under continuous deformations. Betti numbers characterize the connectivity structure: β₀ counts connected components, β₁ counts loops, β₂ counts voids.
The Kuramoto model describes synchronization of coupled oscillators. The order parameter r measures global coherence: r=1 indicates full synchronization, r=0 indicates incoherence.
Attractor dynamics in neural networks describe stable states that the network converges to. Hopfield networks store patterns as fixed-point attractors recoverable from partial information.
Information geometry studies the manifold of probability distributions using Riemannian geometry. The Fisher information metric gives a natural measure of distinguishability between distributions.
Entropy in thermodynamics measures the degree of disorder in a system. The second law states that total entropy of an isolated system never decreases over time.
Phase transitions occur when a physical system changes from one state of matter to another. Order parameters characterize the phases; critical exponents describe the behavior near phase boundaries.
The principle of maximum entropy selects the probability distribution that maximizes entropy subject to known constraints. It represents the least biased inference from incomplete information.
Spectral graph theory studies the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of matrices associated with graphs. The algebraic connectivity (Fiedler value) is the second smallest Laplacian eigenvalue.
Persistent homology tracks topological features across multiple scales. Barcodes encode the birth and death of homological features, providing a multi-scale topological signature.
Manifold learning assumes high-dimensional data lies on a lower-dimensional manifold. Techniques like UMAP and t-SNE project data while preserving local structure.
Reservoir computing uses a fixed recurrent network (reservoir) whose dynamics are read out by a trainable linear layer. Echo state networks and liquid state machines are prominent examples.
Predictive coding proposes that the brain continuously generates predictions about sensory input and updates them based on prediction errors. It implements a form of variational inference.
Renormalization group theory describes how physical systems behave at different length scales. Fixed points of the RG flow correspond to scale-invariant, critical systems.
The Kolmogorov complexity of a string is the length of the shortest program that produces it. This provides a formal measure of the randomness and compressibility of information.

Variational autoencoders learn latent representations by encoding data into a probability distribution and decoding samples from this distribution. The ELBO objective balances reconstruction and regularization.
Counterfactual reasoning asks what would have happened under different circumstances. It is essential for causal attribution, moral responsibility, and planning under uncertainty.

The principle of parsimony (Occam's razor) favors simpler explanations over complex ones when they have equal predictive power. In Bayesian terms, it arises from marginalization over model parameters.
Gödel's incompleteness theorems show that any consistent formal system powerful enough to express arithmetic contains true statements that cannot be proven within the system.
Self-organized criticality describes systems that naturally evolve to a critical state with long-range correlations and power-law statistics, without external tuning.
Formal verification uses mathematical methods to prove the correctness of software or hardware. Model checking exhaustively explores all possible system states to verify temporal logic properties.
The Boltzmann distribution gives the probability of each state in a system at thermal equilibrium. States with lower energy are exponentially more probable at lower temperatures.
Hebbian learning captures the idea that neurons that fire together wire together. It provides a biologically plausible rule for unsupervised learning of correlations in neural networks.
Ergodic theory studies the long-run behavior of dynamical systems. An ergodic system's time averages equal its space averages — it explores its entire state space over time.
The van der Pol oscillator is a nonlinear system with a limit cycle. It exhibits relaxation oscillations and synchronization when coupled to external periodic forcing.
Chaos theory studies deterministic systems with sensitive dependence on initial conditions. The Lyapunov exponent measures the rate of divergence of nearby trajectories.
Stochastic differential equations model systems driven by random noise. The Langevin equation describes Brownian motion as a deterministic drift plus random forcing.
The principle of least action states that physical systems evolve along paths that minimize the action functional. This unifies classical mechanics and gives rise to conservation laws.
Graph neural networks extend neural networks to graph-structured data. Message passing algorithms aggregate information from neighbors to compute node representations.
Algorithmic information theory studies the complexity and randomness of strings using computability theory. Random strings are maximally complex and incompressible.
The Ising model is a mathematical model of ferromagnetism. Spins on a lattice interact with neighbors; phase transitions occur at the critical temperature where long-range order emerges.
Symplectic geometry underlies classical Hamiltonian mechanics. The symplectic form is preserved by Hamiltonian flows, ensuring conservation of phase space volume (Liouville's theorem).
Meta-learning trains models to quickly adapt to new tasks with few examples. Model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) finds initial parameters that are close to optimal for many tasks.
Topological data analysis uses topological invariants to characterize the shape of data. Persistent homology and the mapper algorithm are core TDA methods.
The central limit theorem states that sums of independent random variables converge to a normal distribution as the number of variables grows, regardless of the underlying distribution.
Fourier analysis decomposes signals into sinusoidal components. The discrete Fourier transform enables efficient computation via the fast Fourier transform algorithm.
The Navier-Stokes equations govern the flow of viscous fluids. Turbulence arises from nonlinear instabilities and remains one of the great unsolved problems in physics.
Singular value decomposition factorizes a matrix into orthogonal matrices and a diagonal matrix of singular values. It underlies principal component analysis and low-rank approximation.
Optimal transport measures distances between probability distributions by finding the minimum-cost plan to transport one distribution into another.
The Laplace transform converts differential equations into algebraic equations in the frequency domain. Its inverse recovers the time-domain solution.
Fixed-point theorems guarantee the existence of points that map to themselves under continuous functions. Brouwer's theorem applies to compact convex sets; Banach's to contractions.
The KL divergence measures the information gain from using one probability distribution over another. It is used in variational inference and information theory.
Transfer learning uses knowledge learned on one task to improve performance on a related task. Fine-tuning pre-trained models has become the dominant paradigm in deep learning.
Convergence of iterative algorithms depends on properties of the update rule and the objective function. Gradient descent converges to local minima for smooth objectives under appropriate step sizes.
